*** GILT ADJUDICATION — THE BASIS SWITCHES BACK TO CNBC TONIGHT, AND HERE IS WHY ***
All week CNBC's previous_day_closing on the ten-year gilt was stale or wrong, and Trading Economics was
used to adjudicate. Tonight that has reversed. CNBC now reports the previous close as 5.3721%, which is
effectively the 5.37 this site published at 08:12 this morning — the first time this week its prev field
has agreed with our own published figure. On that basis the ten-year is 5.3819%, up about 0.01.
Trading Economics now says "eased to 5.38% on October 2, 2026, marking a 0.01 percentage points
decrease" — but it said "a 0.02 percentage points decrease" to the same 5.38% level at 08:02 this
morning, so it has revised its own change while holding its level, and its implied previous close is
higher than ours.
*** THE TWO PROVIDERS THEREFORE DISAGREE ON THE SIGN, by about one basis point either way. ***
DECISION: publish 5.38 with +0.01. The principle has not changed — use the provider whose previous close
is demonstrably right — only the provider satisfying it has. This keeps the site's published series
coherent and arithmetically exact: 5.38 -> 5.44 -> 5.48 -> 5.39 -> 5.37 -> 5.38.
The standing rule from 1 October still applies to the THIRTY-year, where the providers disagree more
sharply (CNBC +0.0017 against Trading Economics -0.05): the driver gives its level, 5.8961%, and its
distance below Thursday's 6.029% peak, and asserts no daily direction.

*** GOLD MADE A FRESH HIGH AND REVERSED, FOR THE SECOND TIME THIS WEEK ***
XAU= touched 4,223.95, above the 4,218.16 that was Wednesday's 52-week high, then fell to 4,138.43,
down 0.94% and close to the day's low of 4,125.94. The same pattern — new high, hard reversal — occurred
on Wednesday. Worth saying in the driver without over-reading it.

*** BRENT: FOURTH DAY ON THE DECEMBER CONTRACT, AND A LARGE INTRADAY RANGE ***
@LCO.1 is Dec'26, prev 102.31 (Thursday's settle), finishing effectively flat at 102.39 — but the day's
low was 98.40, almost $4 below the close, so the flat print conceals a round trip. Wednesday evening's
published 103.62 was the NOVEMBER contract and remains non-comparable; the driver says so for the fourth
edition running, per the standing rule.

FX — CLEAN, AND THE BEST AGREEMENT OF THE WEEK. The ECB daily reference rate now exists for today:
Frankfurter gives EUR/GBP 0.85033 dated 2026-10-02 against CNBC's live 0.8505, a gap of about two pips.
Sterling firmed 0.25% to 1.3232 while euro-sterling eased, so sterling was stronger against both.
Yahoo's chart API unusable, ninth day. Investing.com 403s. Reuters returns 401.

THE SHAPE: risk came back. The FTSE recovered 0.32% after Thursday's 1.68% fall, the S&P is up 0.74%,
and the VIX dropped 4% to 15.73, its lowest in over a week. Gilts are steady either side of 5.38% having
been as low as 5.2897% intraday, and the thirty-year is at 5.8961%, more than thirteen basis points below
Thursday's peak. Gold is the one casualty, down 0.94% after a fresh high. Sterling firmer on both crosses.
